Hi Alex / team,

Short answer: deletion of a primary record does NOT typically remove that record from existing immutable snapshots or DR replicas until the snapshot retention/GC window lapses, unless an expedited removal is arranged. Below is the standard behavior and options.

1) Default retention lifecycle (hosted):
- Production data: customer-visible logical deletion is immediate (tombstone + metadata).
- Daily snapshots/point-in-time backups: default retention 90 days for hosted accounts (configurable for enterprise customers). Snapshots are copies of blocks/objects at a point in time; they are immutable for the retention period.
- Offsite DR replicas: replication occurs asynchronously; replication lag can be minutes to hours, but once replicated the snapshot copy follows its own retention policy (typically same 90-day window).
- Object-store garbage collection: if we rely on underlying object storage with versioning, physical object deletion may be deferred until GC/compaction, which can add an additional window (commonly up to 30 days after retention expiry) depending on provider.

2) Why deletion doesn't fully propagate immediately:
- Snapshots reference data by object id; removing a logical record in primary doesn't rewrite past snapshot files.
- Immutable retention prevents accidental data loss for recovery/forensics.

3) Options to meet an erasure request more quickly:
A) Expedited retention shrink: with legal sign-off from both parties and a signed attestation/POA, we can coordinate a manual retention reduction on the tenant's snapshot catalog. This triggers a GC request to the object store. Timelines:
  - Scheduling + approval: 24–72 hours
  - Object-store GC and physical deletion: 48–168 hours (depends on provider and compaction cadence)
  - Total practical window (expedited): ~3–10 days from request to physical deletion, assuming no legal holds.

B) Targeted wipe & re-snapshot (preferred when immediate proof is required):
  - Restore affected snapshot to a sandbox, run a targeted redact/wipe operation, then create a fresh snapshot without the data, and mark the original snapshot for GC.
  - Pros: gives an auditable path and a new snapshot that no longer contains the data.
  - Cons: operationally heavier; requires manual verification and will not retroactively remove the original snapshot until GC finishes. Timeline typically 2–5 days.

C) Customer-controlled Dedicated/Private:
  - For Dedicated or Private deployments where the customer manages backups (on-prem or VPC), the customer has direct control over retention/GC; Redwood can provide runbook steps and remote assistance but cannot force deletion without customer action.

4) Attestation & logs:
- We can produce a timeline-certified attestation stating when we initiated the retention reduction / GC request and when the snapshot manifest was updated.
- Proof of physical deletion is constrained by underlying provider reporting. For hosted accounts we can provide internal GC job logs and object-store deletion confirmations where available. Full third-party audit evidence (e.g., provider irrecoverability certification) may not always be possible.

5) Legal holds & subpoenas:
- Any legal hold will override deletion schedules. If FinPay has an active hold, we cannot remove snapshots until the hold is lifted and documented.

Hi all,

Operational playbook (concise):
1) Triage: confirm exact object ids / user ids and which snapshots reference them (we need a manifest).
2) Approval: require FinPay DPO sign-off + Redwood legal approval (DocuSign link).
3) Execution paths:
   - Path A (expedite retention shrink): update snapshot index -> mark snapshots for immediate GC -> submit GC job to object-store provider.
   - Path B (targeted redact): restore to ephemeral cluster -> run redact job -> take new snapshot -> schedule GC of old snapshot.
4) Verification: we capture GC job id, storage delete-confirmation events, and snapshot-manifest versions. We then produce an internal attestation PDF.

Estimated windows (provider-dependent):
- Admin approval & scheduling: 0.5–3 days
- GC job runtime + provider compaction: 2–7 days
- Attestation generation: same-day after confirmation

Notes:
- For hosted customers on our standard plan the default snapshot retention is 90 days; enterprise customers can request shorter windows or per-account policies.
- If FinPay wants minimal risk to restores, Path B is safer (you get a clean snapshot quickly), but it requires additional infra ops time.
